subject: FinHealth — Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finhealth.com>, Bob Martinez <bob.martinez@finhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FinHealth — Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Hi Alice / Bob — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of needs / pain points (as discussed):
- Regulated PHI workloads: must run in a customer-managed VPC, no egress of raw data to public internet.
- Key management: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) required for model keys and logs.
- Audit & compliance: SOC 2 + HITRUST posture required for any vendor access; retention and audit logs must be exportable.
- Network constraints: strict firewall rules and limited outbound ports; initial deploy may be air-gapped with periodic offline model updates.
- Latency expectations: sub-150ms token latency for core triage workflows; batch embedding jobs for analytics are non-latency sensitive.

Current stack we heard:
- On-prem VPC in Azure (gov tenant), Azure Key Vault in use, internal proxy for outbound traffic, internal SSO via Okta.
- Existing vendor use: embeddings/personalization pipelines using an internal GPU cluster + some managed APIs for non-sensitive data.

Success criteria for pilot (agreed):
1) Private deployment in your VPC with no raw-data egress and customer-managed KMS integration.
2) Demonstrate end-to-end run of triage assistant on a small dataset with latency SLOs met.
3) Auditability: logs and access traces delivered to your SIEM, and evidence for SOC 2 scoping.

Technical constraints / open questions (items we committed to follow up on):
- Exact list of outbound ports allowed from the subnet (Alice to share firewall policy) — affects metrics/exporter connectivity.
- Confirmation whether Azure Key Vault with HSM-backed keys is acceptable, or if you require an on-prem HSM appliance.
- Offline/update cadence: how often can we push model updates into an air-gapped environment? (propose weekly to start).
- Network path for model weights: do you prefer a pull from a secured blob store inside VNet or a push-based model provisioning via customer-controlled jumpbox?

Next steps:
- Alice to share the network egress policy and the Key Vault/HSM contact (by Wed 7/14).
- Redwood (Dylan + Aditya) to draft a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and initial architecture diagram for Private deployment (by Fri 7/16).
- Schedule a technical workshop (Redwood infra + FinHealth infra) to validate firewall rules and KMS integration — propose Tue 7/20 10:00am PT.

Attachments I referenced: FinHealth-IT-Constraints.pdf (high level), example Private/VPC architecture diagram.

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Martinez <bob.martinez@finhealth.com>, procurement@finhealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinHealth — Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Dylan — this is great, appreciate the clear recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- I'll attach our outbound firewall policy and a simplified network diagram (see attached). The policy allows outbound to specific Azure service tags on ports 443 and 22 for management; anything else will need an exception.
- We are on Azure Government; the Key Vault HSM is currently soft-HSM backed, but we have an HA HSM appliance procurement in flight. For the pilot, we could use Azure Key Vault with customer-managed keys if Redwood supports Key Vault integration and the keys never leave our tenancy.
- Air-gap cadence: monthly scheduled updates are preferred for the pilot, with emergency updates via secured jumpbox if needed.
- SOC 2 evidence: our security team will need documentation on access controls and audit log export formats.

We'll aim to share the firewall/export docs by EOD Wed (7/14). Tue 7/20 10am PT works for the tech workshop — please send an invite.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Infrastructure | FinHealth
alice.chen@finhealth.com

Attachments: FinHealth-Network-Diagram.png, FinHealth-IT-Constraints.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@finhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinHealth — Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Adding a few points from product/ops perspective: 
- For KMS: Redwood supports Azure Key Vault integration for Private deployments; keys remain in customer tenancy and can be rotated by you. We'll confirm HSM appliance compatibility (I think we have a partner flow for on-prem HSMs).
- For air-gapped installs: we have an offline bundle option where model artifacts are shipped to an approved blob storage inside your VNet; provisioning can be pull-based from a signed URL or push-based via an Ops jumpbox.
- Regarding latency: we'll size the initial pilot on a dedicated GPU node class that should meet the <150ms token latency for your 1k concurrent user estimate; exact sizing requires request pattern samples (token lengths, concurrency).

I'll pick up drafting the MAP and initial architecture diagram with Dylan — will share a first pass by Fri 7/16.

Thanks —
Marissa
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
